name: Statutory and Other Benefits
text: The Employee shall be entitled to the following benefits during the term of employment: (a) Provident Fund contributions as required under Chapter III of the Code on Social Security, 2020, with both the Employer and Employee contributing at the applicable statutory rates; (b) Employees' State Insurance contributions as required under Chapter IV of the Code on Social Security, 2020, where applicable; (c) Gratuity upon completion of five (5) years of continuous service as required under the Code on Social Security, 2020; (d) Earned Leave of eighteen (18) days per calendar year; (e) Sick Leave of twelve (12) days per calendar year; (f) Public holidays as notified by the Central Government and the applicable State Government; and (g) such other benefits as the Employer may specify in its HR Policy, as amended from time to time. The Employer shall maintain all statutory registers and make all prescribed returns as required under applicable labour laws.

legal_basis.note: Right to payment of maternity benefit
Annual minimum bonus of 8.33 per cent of wages, or one hundred rupees, whichever is higher

invalid_if: PF contributions below statutory minimum of 12% of basic wages
Earned leave entitlement below minimum prescribed under applicable state Shops and Establishments Act
source: Code on Social Security, 2020; Code on Wages, 2019
title: Employee Benefits

jurisdiction_constraints.general: ESI applies where gross salary <= Rs.21,000/month; EPF applies where basic <= Rs.15,000 compulsorily

dispute_hotspots: Gratuity forfeiture disputes — employer incorrectly withholds gratuity pending notice period
EPF exempted trusts — employee claims trust benefits in excess of EPF schedule
Bonus disputes — allegation of improper allocation of bonus
Maternity benefit denial — criminal offence under MBA S.21
authoring_note: LABOUR CODES, 21 NOVEMBER 2025. The four labour Codes were brought into force on 21 November 2025, repealing the 29 central labour statutes this clause previously cited. Chapter references are used for PF and ESI because the operative contribution sections within Chapters III and IV of the CSS Code were not individually verified. The advocate should pin the exact contribution sections. The minimum bonus rate at CoW s.26(1) is unchanged at 8.33 per cent.
